Key responsibilities: 

A. Brand & Client Management:
1. • Act as the primary point of contact for assigned brand accounts, owning the day-to-day relationship end to end. 
2. • Understand each brand's business goals and growth priorities, and translate them into clear, actionable project plans. 
3. • Proactively manage client/brand expectations — communicating progress, risks, and changes before they become problems. 
4. • Identify bottlenecks early and drive them to resolution across internal teams. 

B. Project & Execution Management:
1. • Plan, prioritise, and track multiple concurrent projects and campaigns across brands, timelines, and stakeholders. 
2. • Apply Agile/Scrum thinking to day-to-day execution — sprint planning, task prioritisation, progress tracking, and team coordination — to keep delivery predictable and on schedule. 
3. • Own the delivery calendar for each brand: deadlines, dependencies, approvals, and hand-offs between teams. 
4. • Take full ownership of outcomes — if a deliverable is late, you're the one who knew first and acted fastest. 

C. Cross-Functional Coordination: 
1. • Work closely with performance marketing, creative, content, design, and development teams to ensure every brand requirement is understood and executed correctly. 
2. • Facilitate smooth hand-offs between strategy and execution, ensuring nothing gets lost in translation between the brand's ask and the team's output. 
3. • Run regular syncs/stand-ups with internal teams to track progress and unblock work. 

D. Performance Marketing Coordination:
1. • Maintain working knowledge of Meta Ads, Google Ads, and other relevant digital marketing channels — enough to understand what's being run, why, and how it ties back to brand growth. 
2. • Coordinate with the performance marketing team on campaign calendars, creative requirements, budgets, and reporting timelines. 
3. • Translate campaign performance into brand-level narratives and updates for stakeholders. Reporting & Ownership 
4. • Prepare and present status reports and dashboards to internal leadership and, where required, to brand stakeholders. 
5. • Flag risks to timelines or quality early, with a plan to address them — not just a status update.

3e0602099f3c6c29.description: About StepSecurity StepSecurity prevents, detects, and responds to software supply chain attacks by analyzing behavior across the full software development lifecycle for both developers and AI coding agents. We are building a vertical AI agent for supply chain security across three pillars: securing AI agents on developer machines, OSS package security, and CI/CD security, covering the entire agentic pipeline from dev environment to cloud. Founded by Varun Sharma (ex-Microsoft, 21 years, led supply chain security for Azure) and Ashish Kurmi (ex-Uber, Microsoft, Plaid, 17 years), we are a 16-person team working on hard problems at the intersection of security, AI, and open source. Why this role is exciting We are at the forefront of supply chain security research and product development. We were the first to detect several major supply chain attacks in 2025 and 2026, including the axios npm compromise and tj-actions. (https://www.stepsecurity.io/newsroom) Our research is regularly cited by Bloomberg, TechCrunch, Hacker News, and Dark Reading. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has published advisories citing StepSecurity. (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/09/23/widespread-supply-chain-compromise-impacting-npm-ecosystem) Beyond our enterprise customers, StepSecurity has been adopted by more than 15,000 open-source projects, including projects from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Datadog. You will work on high-impact, zero-to-one problems with meaningful early-stage equity upside. What you'll do Design and build backend services in Golang that power our supply chain security platform. Build scalable, fault-tolerant systems that operate across the full software development lifecycle. Work hands-on in a fast-moving, early-stage environment where you own problems end to end. What we're looking for 2–5 years of experience with strong engineering fundamentals. Golang backend programming experience. Background working with AWS, Azure, or GCP. Experience designing scalable and fault-tolerant systems. Prior early-stage startup experience. An AI-native mindset and comfort in a hands-on, zero-to-one environment. A security background is a plus but not required.
